Vary hypothetical group sizes

Source: R/disperse.R
disperse.Rd

If a study reports a total sample size but no group sizes, these functions generate pairs of hypothetical group sizes that add up to the total:

  • disperse() takes half of an even total and goes up and down from it.

  • disperse2() takes the two consecutive numbers around half of an odd total, and goes down from the lower and up from the upper.

  • disperse_total() takes the total itself and calls one of the two, depending on whether it is even or odd.

They are the basis of grim_map_total_n() and the other functions made by function_map_total_n().

Usage

disperse(n, dispersion = 0:5, n_min = 1L, n_max = NULL, constant = NULL)

disperse2(n, dispersion = 0:5, n_min = 1L, n_max = NULL, constant = NULL)

disperse_total(n, dispersion = 0:5, n_min = 1L, n_max = NULL, constant = NULL)

Arguments

n

Numeric. In disperse(), half of an even total. In disperse2(), the two consecutive numbers closest to half of an odd total, such as c(25, 26) for 51. In disperse_total(), the total itself.

dispersion

Numeric. Non-negative whole numbers of steps up and down from n (or, in disperse_total(), from half of n). Default is 0:5.

n_min

Numeric. Minimal group size. Default is 1L.

n_max

Numeric. Maximal group size. Default is NULL, no maximum.

constant

Optionally, a length-2 vector, or a list of such vectors (which includes a data frame with two rows), to repeat alongside each pair of group sizes. Default is NULL.

Value

A tibble with these columns:

  • n: the group sizes. Each pair of consecutive rows adds up to the total.

  • n_change: the number of steps from the input n, negative for the lower group size of each pair.

Details

A pair with a group size below n_min or above n_max is dropped. Columns from constant are named after a named list's elements, or "constant1", "constant2", etc. for an unnamed one; a single pair is "constant".

References

Bauer, P. J., & Francis, G. (2021). Expression of Concern: Is It Light or Dark? Recalling Moral Behavior Changes Perception of Brightness. Psychological Science, 32(12), 2042–2043. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/09567976211058727

See also

function_map_total_n() and grim_map_total_n().

Examples

# For a total of 40, `n` is 20:
disperse(n = 20)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 2
#>        n n_change
#>    <int>    <int>
#>  1    20        0
#>  2    20        0
#>  3    19       -1
#>  4    21        1
#>  5    18       -2
#>  6    22        2
#>  7    17       -3
#>  8    23        3
#>  9    16       -4
#> 10    24        4
#> 11    15       -5
#> 12    25        5

disperse(n = 20, dispersion = c(3, 6, 10))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>       n n_change
#>   <int>    <int>
#> 1    17       -3
#> 2    23        3
#> 3    14       -6
#> 4    26        6
#> 5    10      -10
#> 6    30       10

# For an odd total, `disperse2()` takes two group sizes:
disperse2(n = c(25, 26))
#> # A tibble: 12 × 2
#>        n n_change
#>    <int>    <int>
#>  1    25        0
#>  2    26        0
#>  3    24       -1
#>  4    27        1
#>  5    23       -2
#>  6    28        2
#>  7    22       -3
#>  8    29        3
#>  9    21       -4
#> 10    30        4
#> 11    20       -5
#> 12    31        5

# `disperse_total()` takes the total itself:
disperse_total(n = 40)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 2
#>        n n_change
#>    <int>    <int>
#>  1    20        0
#>  2    20        0
#>  3    19       -1
#>  4    21        1
#>  5    18       -2
#>  6    22        2
#>  7    17       -3
#>  8    23        3
#>  9    16       -4
#> 10    24        4
#> 11    15       -5
#> 12    25        5
disperse_total(n = 51)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 2
#>        n n_change
#>    <int>    <int>
#>  1    25        0
#>  2    26        0
#>  3    24       -1
#>  4    27        1
#>  5    23       -2
#>  6    28        2
#>  7    22       -3
#>  8    29        3
#>  9    21       -4
#> 10    30        4
#> 11    20       -5
#> 12    31        5

# Values that repeat alongside the pairs:
disperse_total(37, constant = c("5.24", "3.80"))
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>        n n_change constant
#>    <int>    <int> <chr>   
#>  1    18        0 5.24    
#>  2    19        0 3.80    
#>  3    17       -1 5.24    
#>  4    20        1 3.80    
#>  5    16       -2 5.24    
#>  6    21        2 3.80    
#>  7    15       -3 5.24    
#>  8    22        3 3.80    
#>  9    14       -4 5.24    
#> 10    23        4 3.80    
#> 11    13       -5 5.24    
#> 12    24        5 3.80    

df_constant <- tibble::tibble(
  name = c("Paul", "Mathilda"), age = 27:28,
  registered = c(TRUE, FALSE)
)
disperse_total(37, constant = df_constant)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 5
#>        n n_change name       age registered
#>    <int>    <int> <chr>    <int> <lgl>     
#>  1    18        0 Paul        27 TRUE      
#>  2    19        0 Mathilda    28 FALSE     
#>  3    17       -1 Paul        27 TRUE      
#>  4    20        1 Mathilda    28 FALSE     
#>  5    16       -2 Paul        27 TRUE      
#>  6    21        2 Mathilda    28 FALSE     
#>  7    15       -3 Paul        27 TRUE      
#>  8    22        3 Mathilda    28 FALSE     
#>  9    14       -4 Paul        27 TRUE      
#> 10    23        4 Mathilda    28 FALSE     
#> 11    13       -5 Paul        27 TRUE      
#> 12    24        5 Mathilda    28 FALSE
